name: Chat

frontend_tools.name: view_artifact
frontend_tools.description: See an artifact as the user sees it, as a PNG image, to check your work: a diagram, table or render_ui item shown in this conversation, or Mermaid or HTML you pass here, which the user does not see. Without arguments: the newest artifact. `id`: a render_ui id (see harness_info) or an artifact key. `kind`: the newest of that kind. The result also has Mermaid syntax errors and the script errors of Html frames. Uses the app's current theme. The app window must be open.

html.description: HTML to draw, in the same sandboxed frame as render_ui Html

frontend_tools.name: render_ui
frontend_tools.description:
Show rich, optionally interactive content to the user: cards, grids, lists, tables, charts, diffs, file links, timelines, traces, logs, images, stats, tabs, steppers, accordions, choices, checkboxes, inputs, buttons. Input: {"root": node, "placement"?, "id"?, "title"?, "icon"?}. A node is {"type", "props", "children"?, "on"?, "visible"?}; only Stack, Card, Repeat, Popover, Tabs, Stepper, Accordion and Grid take children.
Placement: inline in the chat (default) or a live area: top, bottom, or a panel at the left or right (needs an id and a title, an icon is optional; right opens in the top right zone, left in the top left; the user can move it). A call with the same id replaces that item; {"id", "remove": true} removes it.
Session State: any prop can be {"$state": "/path"}, {"$template": "Branch: ${/setup/branch}"} or {"$computed": "count", "args": {"values": {"$state": "/checks"}, "eq": true}} (also "length" and "sum") and updates when the state changes (change it with state_patch). Choice and Input write the user's input with {"$bindState": "/path"}. on.press/change/submit/finish run actions: {"action": "setState"|"pushState", "params": {"statePath", "value"}}, {"action": "removeState", "params": {"statePath", "index"?}}, {"action": "sendMessage", "params": {"text"}} (sends the text to you as the user's next message; text can be a $template), {"action": "js", "params": {"statePath", "code"}} (runs JavaScript, an expression or a function body with return, with `state` in scope, and writes its result to statePath; actions in a list see the writes before them). JavaScript ($js, js) runs sandboxed in the app without you, e.g. a calculator or a converter: no DOM, network or timers, 50 ms at most, JSON in and out. "visible" shows a node only when the state says so, e.g. {"$state": "/setup/target"} (picked) or {"$state": "/setup/step", "eq": 2}. The user's state changes do not reach you by themselves: add a sendMessage when you must react.
Data from state: Repeat renders its children per item of a state array; inside, {"$item": "field"}, {"$index": true}, "${field}" in a $template, {"$bindItem": "field"}, visible {"$item": "field", "eq"?}; in actions, statePath {"$item": "field"} and removeState index {"$index": true}. When the data changes, patch the state instead of sending the tree again.
Layout: compose generic parts (Stack with direction, align, justify, wrap, fill; Card variants; Text for short labels, numbers and arrows between parts; Table cells and KeyValue values with a tone) instead of asking for a special component.
Keep related parts in one item: Tabs for parts in any order, a Stepper for steps in order (a setup, a review, a quiz). A Choice whose pick can be checked takes `answer`, `result` and `explanation`.
Html: only for diagrams and custom visuals the catalog cannot show (architecture diagrams, annotated drawings); it runs in a sandboxed frame with the app's theme colors as CSS variables. Attributes: data-state="/path" (shows the value as text), data-visible='{"$state": "/path", "eq": "x"}' (same syntax as visible), data-on-click='<action or array>' and data-on-change (run actions), data-bind="/path" on input, select and textarea (two-way; writes on change: blur, Enter or toggle). Scripts get window.harness: `state` (the whole Session State, replaced on each change), `get(path)` (the value at a JSON Pointer, e.g. get('/arch/selected')), `subscribe(fn)` (calls fn(state) at once and after each change; returns an unsubscribe function), `patch(ops)` (JSON Patch ops, e.g. [{op: 'replace', path: '/arch/selected', value: 'api'}]; replace also creates missing keys), `send(text)` (a user message to you), `run(actions)` (render_ui actions, as in on.press). Prefer get and subscribe over keeping your own copy. Set data in the state with state_patch first, then draw from it in subscribe; patch the state later instead of sending new HTML. Leave height out: the frame fits its content.
Short text props (table cells and headings, KeyValue, List items, Choice labels, Card descriptions) take inline Markdown: `code`, **bold**, *italic*, links.
Use it for results, status, comparisons, screenshots, decisions you need from the user, or guided tasks, instead of a long plain message.
Icons (the icon prop): check, x, alert, info, help, file, folder, code, terminal, bug, test, package, git-branch, git-commit, git-pull-request, git-merge, rocket, server, database, globe, lock, key, user, users, clock, calendar, search, link, settings, star, zap, list, message, chart.
Components:
- Stack(direction?: vertical|horizontal, gap?: sm|md|lg, align?: start|center|end|stretch, justify?: start|center|end|between, wrap?, fill?) + children: Lays out children vertically (default) or in a row. In a row, children share the width (badges, buttons, Text keep theirs); `fill: false` lets each keep its own width. `align`/`justify` place them, `wrap: false` keeps one line.
- Card(title?, description?, tone?: neutral|info|success|warning|error, icon?, variant?: default|compact|plain) + children: A bordered box with an optional header (title, description, icon) and tone; holds children. variant: default, compact (less padding, e.g. small boxes in a row) or plain (no border or background: a titled section).
- Markdown(text): Markdown text. A ```mermaid fence draws a diagram; a ```ansi fence shows terminal colors.
- Text(text, tone?: neutral|info|success|warning|error, mono?, size?: xs|sm|md|lg, muted?, weight?: normal|medium|bold, tooltip?): Short plain text: a label, a number, an arrow or a caption between other components. No Markdown (use Markdown for prose).
- Repeat(items, key?, empty?, direction?: vertical|horizontal, gap?: sm|md|lg, align?: start|center|end|stretch, justify?: start|center|end|between, wrap?, fill?) + children: Renders its children once per item of a state array (`items`: {"$state": "/path"}), laid out like a Stack. Inside, {"$item": "field"} reads the item ("" the whole item), {"$index": true} its index, a $template takes "${field}", {"$bindItem": "field"} writes to it, and visible takes {"$item": "field", "eq"?}. `key` names an item field that identifies it; `empty` is shown when there are no items.
- KeyValue(items): Label/value rows; a value can take a `tone`, `mono` and a `tooltip`.
- Table(columns, rows, sortable?, filter?): A table: column headings and rows. A row is an array of cells, or {cells, tone} to tint the row. A cell is text, or {text, tone?, mono?, icon?, tooltip?}. `sortable` sorts by a clicked column; `filter` adds a search box (both use the cell text).
- Badge(text, tone?: neutral|info|success|warning|error, icon?, tooltip?): A short label, e.g. a status.
- Code(code, language?): A code block.
- Image(src, alt, caption?): One image; the user can open it full size.
- Carousel(images): Several images, one at a time, with previous/next.
- Stat(label, value, hint?, tone?: neutral|info|success|warning|error, tooltip?): One number or short value with a label, e.g. a count, a total or a status.
- Progress(value, max?, label?): A progress bar from 0 to max (default 100).
- Choice(options, value: $bindState, answer?, result?: $bindState, explanation?, columns?: 1|2, variant?: list|buttons|select): Options to pick one from (distinct values); writes the picked value to `value` ($bindState). When a pick can be checked, set `answer` to the expected value: after a pick it shows right/wrong, locks, writes true/false to `result` ($bindState) and shows `explanation`. `on.change` runs after a pick. on: change.
- Input(value: $bindState, label?, placeholder?, multiline?): A text field; writes its text to its $bindState path. `multiline` for longer text. `on.submit` runs on Enter (Cmd/Ctrl+Enter when multiline). on: submit.
- Button(label, variant?: primary|secondary|outline|ghost, disabled?, icon?, tooltip?): A button; `on.press` runs its actions. A Grid of only Buttons is a keypad: exactly `columns` wide, keys fill their cells. on: press.
- Popover(label?, icon?, variant?: primary|secondary|outline|ghost, title?, width?: sm|md|lg) + children: A click opens a small floating box with the children: details, a form or actions next to the thing they belong to. The trigger is a button from `label` (+ `icon`, `variant`); without `label`, the first child is the trigger (e.g. a Badge or Text; not a Button) and the other children are the content. State, bindings and actions work inside, also in a Repeat. Closes on a click outside or Escape.
- Tabs(tabs, value?: $bindState) + children: Tabs: one child per tab, one shown at a time; for parts the user browses in any order. `value` ($bindState, optional) holds the open tab's index.
- Stepper(steps, value?: $bindState) + children: Steps shown one at a time with Back/Next, e.g. a setup, a review of findings, or a quiz: one child per step. `value` ($bindState, optional) holds the step index. `on.finish` runs when the user presses Finish on the last step. on: finish.
- Diff(patch?, path?, old?, new?): A code diff, highlighted. Give `patch` (a unified git diff; several files are fine) or `path` with `old` and `new` text. File names open the file in the user's editor.
- List(items, check?: $bindState): Rich rows: title, description, meta text, icon, badge, tooltip. `status` (done, running, waiting, blocked, failed) shows a status icon in place of `icon`. With `check` ($bindState to an object), each row gets a checkbox that writes `{ [id]: true|false }` there, e.g. a todo list; `on.change` runs after a toggle. Status and check are independent: the checkbox comes first, the status icon after it. on: change.
- Checkbox(label, description?, value: $bindState): One checkbox; writes true/false to `value` ($bindState). `on.change` runs after a toggle. on: change.
- Switch(label, description?, value: $bindState): An on/off switch; writes true/false to `value` ($bindState). `on.change` runs after a toggle. on: change.
- Accordion(items, multiple?, open?) + children: Collapsible sections: one child per item, titled by `items`. `multiple` lets several stay open; `open` lists indexes open at first.
- Timeline(items): Events in order: title, description, time, tone, icon. E.g. a deploy history or the steps of an investigation.
- Chart(type: bar|line|area|pie, data, x, series, stacked?, height?): A chart of `data` (rows of objects; bindable). `x` names the label key, `series` the numeric keys to plot. type: bar, line, area or pie (pie uses the first series).
- Grid(columns?: 2|3|4|5|6) + children: Children in up to `columns` equal columns (default 3); fewer when the area is narrow. E.g. a row of Stats. Only Buttons: a keypad, always `columns` wide.
- Log(text, title?): Terminal or log output with its ANSI colors, in a scrolling box that starts at the end. `title` names it, e.g. the command.
- Trace(spans, unit?): A trace waterfall: spans with `start` and `duration` (same unit, e.g. ms) and an optional `parent` id, drawn as bars on one time axis. E.g. a request's steps or a build's phases.
- FileLink(path, line?, label?): A link that opens a file of the workspace, at a line, in the user's editor. `path` is relative to the workspace (or absolute inside it).
- PullRequest(repo, number, title, state: open|draft|merged|closed, url?, head?, base?, author?, updated?, additions?, deletions?, files?, commits?, checks?, review?: approved|changes_requested|required|none, labels?, note?, variant?: summary|card|compact): A GitHub pull request: state, title, branches, +/- stats, checks, review. variant: summary (default), card or compact.
- Html(html, height?, title?): Free HTML/SVG in a sandboxed frame, for diagrams and custom visuals the catalog cannot show (e.g. an architecture diagram). Prefer catalog components for normal UI. Connects to the Session State with data-* attributes and `window.harness` (see above).

id.description: Names this item: a later call with the same id replaces it. Required for top, bottom, left and right.

placement.description: Where it shows: inline in the chat (default), or in a live area of the chat: top, bottom, or a panel on the left or right side (the user can move it to any other zone).

title.description: Label of the left or right panel.

icon.description: Icon of the left or right panel, in the panel strip.

remove.description: Remove the item with this id.

expr.description: Read from the Session State: {"$state": "/path"}, {"$template": "Done: ${/checks/done}"}, {"$computed": "count"|"length"|"sum", "args": {"values", "eq"?}}, or {"$js": "JavaScript"} (an expression or a function body with return; `state` is the Session State). Inside a Repeat: {"$item": "field"} and {"$index": true}.

visible.description: Show the node only when true: {"$state": "/path"} (truthy), with "eq", "neq" or "not": true; inside a Repeat also {"$item": "field"} or {"$index": true}; {"$and": [...]}, {"$or": [...]}; or a boolean.

bind.description: Two-way binding: {"$bindState": "/path"}; inside a Repeat, {"$bindItem": "field"} for a field of the item.

path.description: A state path; inside a Repeat, {"$item": "field"} for a field of the item.

children.description: Only for Stack, Card, Repeat, Popover, Tabs, Stepper, Accordion and Grid.

instructions:
This Frontend is a chat. It renders your messages as Markdown.

- Inline code that looks like code (calls, objects, arrows) is highlighted in the language of the message's code blocks or file names, else TypeScript. When that would be wrong, prefix it with `{:lang}`, e.g. `{:rust}Vec<u8>` or `{:bash}git log`; `{:plain}` turns highlighting off.
- Pull request refs become chips with title and status, but only explicit ones: `owner/repo#123` for any repository, or `PR #123` (or `PR#123`) for this Session's repository. A bare `#123` stays plain text (it may be a list item), so never use it for a PR.
- To show structured results to the user (a summary of a task, a comparison, a table, status, screenshots or other images), call the `render_ui` tool instead of writing a long plain message. Keep plain text for short answers and explanations.
- `render_ui` takes a nested tree, not a flat element map: `{"root": {"type": "Card", "props": {"title": "Summary"}, "children": [{"type": "Markdown", "props": {"text": "..."}}, {"type": "Table", "props": {"columns": ["PR", "Size"], "rows": [["#15", "+1023"]]}}]}}`. Its description lists all components and props; if a call is rejected, the error repeats it.
- When you point the user at code, use a `FileLink` (path and line) or a `Diff`: the user can open the file in their editor from there.
- `render_ui` images can be local file paths (for example screenshots you made); the Harness copies them, so they stay visible later. Use a carousel for several images.
- Live areas: `render_ui` with a `placement` of `top`, `bottom`, `left` or `right` (a panel on that side, with a `title` and an optional `icon`; the user can move it) and an `id` keeps content visible outside the message flow while you work, such as progress, a checklist, or a panel the user works in. Call it again with the same `id` to replace it, or with `"remove": true` to remove it.
- Input from the user: when you need a decision or details (pick an approach, confirm a plan, fill in names or options), a Choice, Input or Button is often clearer than asking in text. Keep the data in the Session State and bind components to it (`{"$state": "/path"}`, `{"$template": "..."}`, `{"$computed": "count", ...}`); Choice and Input write with `$bindState`. State changes alone do not reach you: add a `sendMessage` action (on a Button, a Choice's `on.change`, or a Stepper's `on.finish`) where you must react. Change the state yourself with `state_patch`.
- Keep related content together: one item with Tabs (parts to compare or browse in any order) or a Stepper (steps done in order, such as a setup, a review of findings, or a quiz; its Next button moves on) instead of one item per part.
- Use `visible` to show something only when it fits, for example a next step after a choice is made, or a summary on the last step.
- When a pick can be checked (a quiz, a known correct option), give the Choice the expected value as `answer`, a `result` path and an `explanation`: it marks right or wrong itself, and `$computed` `count` over the results gives a total.
- Choice option values must be distinct and name the option; never use them to encode a verdict. Use object keys (`/review/findings/f1`), not array indexes, for values the UI writes.
- When the UI should react without you (a calculator, a converter, a filter, totals), compute it with `{"$js": "..."}` values and `{"action": "js", "params": {"statePath", "code"}}` actions: sandboxed JavaScript with `state` in scope that runs in the app. A Grid of only Buttons is a keypad.
- Build layouts from the generic parts: Stack (`align`, `justify`, `wrap`, `fill: false` to keep children at their own width), Card variants, `Text` for short labels, numbers and arrows, Table cells and KeyValue values with a `tone`. For lists from data, keep the array in the Session State and render it with `Repeat` (`$item`, `$index`, `$bindItem` inside); when the data changes, patch the state instead of sending the tree again.
- Put secondary detail in a `tooltip` (Badge, Stat, Button, Text, KeyValue values, List items, Table cells); it shows on hover or focus, not on touch, so never put needed information only there. For details or actions that belong to one item, use a `Popover` (opens on click).
- For a diagram or custom visual the catalog cannot show (an architecture diagram, an annotated drawing), use `Html`: your HTML/SVG in a sandboxed frame. Connect it to the Session State with `data-state`, `data-visible`, `data-on-click`, `data-bind` or `window.harness` (`state`, `subscribe`, `patch`, `send`, `run`). The frame has no network: no remote images, fonts or scripts; draw with inline SVG or `data:` images. Prefer the catalog components for normal UI.
- To check a diagram or HTML you made (does it parse, does it look right), call `view_artifact`: it returns a PNG of it as the user would see it, with any errors. Pass new `mermaid` or `html` to check it before the user sees it.
